focus: cli-external-orchestration and cli-classifier hubs with their mode packets
noveltyJustification: Seven of seven findings are new: no prior lineage covered the CLI hubs, and the alias-drift counts were measured this iteration.
ruledOut: Treating mode-packet INTENT_SIGNALS as a duplicate of hub INTENT_SIGNALS

label: cli-external-orchestration restates executor vocabulary in four machine-readable places (mode-registry aliases, hub-router vocabularyClasses, ROUTER INTENT_SIGNALS, packet Keywords comments) and the lists already disagree: 6 opencode registry aliases are absent from ROUTER and 8 devin ROUTER keywords are absent from the registry.

Stage-two leaf routing has three disagreeing definitions per mode: ROUTER.md first slice is cli-reference plus integration-patterns, cli-devin ALWAYS is cli-reference plus prompt-quality-card, and its GENERATION RESOURCE_MAP is cli-reference plus prompt-templates.
All seven mode packets carry a full Python router and the same six-step call sequence; the shared helper reference still says six cli-* siblings and omits cli-hermes, which defers to it.
cli-classifier restates the Jev vocabulary four times, and its hub ROUTER DEFAULT_RESOURCE=[] contradicts the packet's two-file DEFAULT_RESOURCES baseline.

The advisor stage-one input duplicates the same phrases a fifth time: 73 intent_signals and 87 derived trigger_phrases in cli-external-orchestration graph-metadata, plus description keywords and 33 classifier intent_signals.
ROUTER.md is enforced through leaf-manifest.json, not the benchmark; the SKILL.md claim that benchmarks parse the block is stale because the Lane C harness was removed.

Both hubs put long compound routing prose before the instructions: 27 lines over 200 characters in the hub SKILL.md with a 779-character sentence at line 76, and 47 such lines in cli-devin with a 1,397-character rule at line 333.
